messages:
alex.k: Quick sanity check — bringing up Ceres-7B with INT8 weight-only. Did a quick bitsandbytes vs llm.int8 run land yet? Looking for perf vs quality to decide canary strategy.
maria.t: Ran an initial bakeoff on p4d. Quick numbers: bnb int8: median latency ~86ms @16 tokens, p95 ~230ms, throughput ~320 tok/s. llm.int8: median ~95ms, p95 ~260ms, throughput ~290 tok/s. GPU mem: bnb ~9.2GB, llm.int8 ~8.8GB. Rough but consistent across 3 runs.
raj.p: Quality summary on our instruction QA set: bnb shows ~0.9% absolute top-1 accuracy drop vs fp16, llm.int8 ~1.3% drop. On the multi-turn date/entity slice bnb has a ~2% regression (hallucinated dates). Will paste examples.
sam.o: can you share the exact quant config and command used? was this AWQ/GPTQ or the classic bitsandbytes weight-only?
maria.t: bench command we used: 
```
python bench.py --model ceres-7b --quant bnb --batch 8 --seq 128 --framework triton
```
config notes: `bnb.8bit=weight_only, groups=128` for bnb. llm.int8 run used `llm_int8=True, qtype=\"per-channel\"`.
jen.l: interesting that bnb is faster but slightly worse on some slices. Could tokenizer/decoder bias explain this? @kai.z any traces from decode logs? :thinking_face:
kai.z: saw a token alignment oddity in the multi-turn trace. Example: `tokenizer.encode("Jan 5, 2026")` produced different splits post-quant for one session which then changed subsequent decoding probs — looks like small logit bias accumulating over turns. Pushing a unit test now.
infra-bot: Deploy job r-ceres-int8-bench started on p4d-2x (run id r-4523).
ci-bot: Full eval artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/artifacts/r-4523 (private). Snippet of eval table: 
- FP16 baseline: top1 87.4%, ppl 12.1
- bnb int8: top1 86.5%, ppl 12.9
- llm.int8: top1 86.1%, ppl 13.4
(These are aggregated numbers across our 12K eval prompts)
raj.p: quick examples attached inline: 
1) prompt: \"When was Acme founded?\" fp16 -> \"2009\"; bnb -> \"2009\"; llm.int8 -> \"2010\" (off by year)
2) multi-turn chat where follow-up asks about timeline: fp16 coherent; bnb sometimes inserts an extra year token in 2/100 cases.
alex.k: So risk profile: bnb gives ~10% perf throughput win and lower median latency but a small accuracy hit on sensitive NER/date slices. We should gate if absolute drop >1.0% on critical slices. Thoughts on rollout?
sam.o: Proposed rollout: canary 5% traffic to int8, 95% to fp16, with fallback to fp16 if exact-match on key slices drops >0.8% for 10m window. I can open PR for the route policy. :thumbsup:
maria.t: did one extra run with groups=64 for bnb: accuracy improved by ~0.3% (top1 86.8%) but mem +300MB and median latency +8ms. So there is a knob tradeoff.
jen.l: can we surface p95/p99 by prompt-length bucket in Console? That would help decide which customer routes are safe. cc @product\.
alex.k: Action items: sam -> rollout PR + policy, kai -> tokenization unit tests and trace dump, maria -> re-run full eval with groups=64 and upload artifact, raj -> collate failing prompts into INF ticket. I'll create INF-1245 and link artifacts. Thanks all.
kai.z: starting tokenization test now, will post results here. :mag:
sam.o: I'll draft the canary config: route 5% to 'ceres-int8-bnb-g64' variant, 95% to 'ceres-fp16', metric watches: exact_match and p95 latency. On breach -> automatic rollback.
maria.t: noted — will push eval artifact once done (expect ~45m run).
alex.k: perfect. we'll reconvene after the full eval. :rocket:
